Main finding: observed images can fit well while fixed-camera views still fragment. Better local flow or geometry losses have not established identity recovery across occlusion.
Last week: stronger image candidates, physics issues exposed

Color-repaired C1 became a common control. H3 combined coverage and local strain, raising historical-protocol test PSNR from 40.3721 to 40.8782 dB. Shared stiffness, soft object groups and later regularizers brought no consistent overall gain. Frozen-trajectory velocity fitting exposed possible internal-clock aliasing. [02-11]
This week: turn visual impressions into checkable evidence

Flow, velocity, shared-stress and momentum comparisons were completed, alongside local image-object / surface-bank / Gaussian-row associations. Fixed-camera scans showed that original-trajectory RGB scores do not establish novel-view completeness. Conditional S1-S6 training and evaluation are complete: S6 improves observed images and trajectory fits, but fixed novel views still fragment. [12-38]

Dark patches at high alpha can reflect color or occlusion errors and are excluded from transparent-hole rates. Old C1 clamped the red channel to zero in a difficult yellow ROI, motivating color-gradient repair before further point insertion. [02,03]
After repair: retain new C1 as the image baseline
Softplus color + weaker mask + foreground RGB
Adds weak affine term; coverage improves, RGB declines
Adds 298 points; no stable overall gain over C2

Color repair is a package of changes; its full gain cannot be attributed to Softplus alone. New vs old C1 gains 4.6262 dB PSNR, but mask IoU drops from 0.9764 to 0.9161 and background spill rises to 1.004%. [03]
Centroid: a higher mean does not mean every frame improves

G0 to G1: PSNR 37.1394 to 37.5279 dB; centroid distance 121.52 to 0.56 px. SSIM and LPIPS worsen; only 23/50 frames gain PSNR, with median delta -0.1319 dB. The earliest three frames drive most of the gain. A global alpha centroid does not constrain local shape, depth or identity. [04]

Date supplement: the 10/26 time-split V3/V4 retrainings reached final PSNR 40.0917/40.1055 dB. The kinematic term added only 0.0138 dB with mixed perceptual results. These runs differ from C0 on this page; values are not interchangeable. [01]
Isotropy: scratch controls show no overall improvement

On 10/26, both arms started at the same random step0 and ran 50k. iso=0 to 0.001 changed PSNR 39.7240 to 39.5581 dB and legacy LPIPS 0.0106815 to 0.0111843; SSIM and MS-SSIM rose slightly. An earlier continuation was saved and stopped after 10,489 extra control steps and 1000 isotropy steps. It has no final comparison and is not counted as a negative result. [01]
Same 50 historical test images, final50k, legacy LPIPS. Low coverage is the percentage of the GT core with alpha<0.9.
Coverage partly improves; image quality declines
Accepted candidate; PSNR improves on 33/50 frames
Slightly higher mean; tail / validation guard fails
H3 vs C1: PSNR +0.5061 dB; low coverage down 33.24%; background spill 1.0041% to 0.8036%. Observed-image proxies improve; complete 3D geometry is not established.

H3 still has severe failures: original frame85 is 6.2382 dB below C1. D1 partly repairs it, but the worst-five-frame mean drops from H3's 34.1705 to 33.8594 dB. A +0.0376 dB test mean cannot override the predefined validation selection. [05-08]

R1 quaternion normalization reached 50k with validation PSNR 40.1520 dB; test scores are unavailable. R2 difficult-frame sampling was saved and stopped at 31,900 steps. R3 and H5 did not run. Some runs diverged before new modules activated, so final deltas cannot all be read as single-component causal effects. [08]
Three questions: do material constraints help, do soft groups represent objects, and can an independent velocity field fit rendered motion?
This experiment's control; not the 40.3721 C1 run
Worse on 49/50 frames; E only 1 to 0.99348

Local dL/dF has a heavy tail: P2 peaks near 187,195. This is a local F derivative, not a model-weight gradient. The global effective-material prior is not a default improvement; the small E change does not establish material identification. [09]

Object grouping: frozen geometry groups O1 and learnable O2 achieve test PSNR 38.8108/38.4809 dB, both below reused C1. Learnable assignments remain diffuse across 16 occupied slots. RGB gradients and slot use do not prove true object IDs. This diagnostic grouping is distinct from known material regions. [10]
Fit velocity to frozen H3 trajectories: completed 11/1

Relative RMSE uses frozen trajectory derivatives as the teacher; zero velocity is 100%. A small sample can be fitted, ruling out a completely broken gradient. A monotonic clock greatly improves time holdout, but transfer across IDs remains poor. [11]

Two distant times map to nearly the same internal scalar time despite different target velocities. A monotonic-clock control supports aliasing / conditioning as one bottleneck. It uses no true velocity GT and yields no new image-quality gain. B3 random initialization gives 68.84%/91.73% training / time-holdout error, leaving this interpretation unchanged. [11]
A Shared Trajectory Is Not Enough
J1 spans the weeks; K/L/M/N completed on 11/2. The table reports test results at each run's best checkpoint selected by validation PSNR.
Final internal velocity mismatch still 99.73%; images below H3
Images recover vs L1; momentum residual unresolved
Motion slightly better; cross-time momentum gate fails
K motivated corrections to the auxiliary flow pipeline

The PIDG loader's FoV ordering differs from the standard metadata convention. CUDA mean-pixel offset signs and transmittance T before / after alpha compositing also affect flow. V2 diagnostic corrections raise coverage from about 48%-50% to above 99%. K training used V1, so its degradation alone cannot reject trajectory-derived velocity or flow direction. [13]
L isolates the effect of shared stress

L0/L1 both correct the flow / camera helpers and derive velocity from the full center R(q)X+b; only the stress source changes. L1 adds just 0.0198 dB validation PSNR and reduces velocity-step EPE by 0.12%, below the predefined 10% motion gate. The new shared head updates; legacy physics networks are frozen by protocol, not omitted accidentally from the optimizer. [14]

When v is defined from the same trajectory, zero internal v=dx/dt error follows by construction. Correct velocity, stress divergence and image fitting still require independent observations and stable numerics.
Rows are not a common-architecture ranking: K to L also fixes helpers; L to M changes backward gradients; M to N changes time discretization and spatial derivatives. M/N details follow. [12-16]
Momentum experiments retain the actual forward residual. Smaller backward gradients are not reported as smaller physical errors.
M1: protect shared parameters from momentum gradients

The weighted momentum gradient on shared deformation parameters is capped at 10% of the same-batch RGB gradient. Private stress-head and original strain-rate coefficient gradients remain. Vs L1, best test PSNR rises 33.9658 to 39.7018 dB and velocity-step EPE falls 0.8363 to 0.7611 px (8.99%), short of the predefined 10% gate. [15]

On a common 64-point probe at frame83, momentum RMS is about 4711.6, original strain-rate correction divergence about 4734.3, and direct stress divergence only 0.075. This points to rate correction / spatial derivatives and gradient competition, not proof that missing external force is the cause. Curves differ before the first momentum event, preventing strict single-factor attribution of all image recovery. [15]
N1: consistent intervals and local quadratic derivatives

The frame83 anomaly eases, but both operators worsen at frame2; the 25% cross-time momentum gate fails. Results remain sensitive to time-difference step and neighborhood. Retain as a numerical-compatibility candidate, not a physics success. [16]
Direct flow ablation with the original C1 structure

Velocity stepping improves 16.43%, but the 0.3705 dB validation PSNR loss exceeds the 0.2 dB guard; overall benefit is false. Gains mainly affect the separate velocity branch, not deformation trajectories. This flow O1 differs from last week's object-group O1. [17]

Association checks source / target centers, complete alpha x T footprints, segment purity and original bidirectional flow. Old rasterizer metadata stores only the first 20 contributors per pixel. Full group-compositing audits avoid treating truncated normalized shares as total contributions. [18-23]

Apart from P1's first 13k additional training steps, this page mainly covers data, inference and correspondence diagnostics without Gaussian optimization. Implementing and verifying local correspondence does not establish a new PSNR gain. Separate silhouettes, stable group numbers and overlapping Gaussian row IDs do not prove true material-point identity. [18-23]
Cleaner Local Links, No Lasting Support
Completed 11/2: T0/T1 each add 2000 updates to the same full C1 50k state, reaching 52k; 86,143 points and 2065 anchors.
Mean points supported by center and footprint

Local purity improves while total contribution shrinks. At every evaluated training time from original frame82 onward, the early bank loses support for visible ducks. The temporal association term is zero on all 29 late training-frame pairs. Visible flow supplies no independent identity bridge across complete occlusion. [24]

Thin area is measured by a radius-2-pixel morphological opening of alpha>0.5 support at 400x225. Small islands, enclosed holes and boundary complexity are also recorded. Missing coverage, low core alpha, background spill and IoU are computed only where real observations exist. [26]

Metrics track behavior; losses affect training. Novel-view proxies without GT cannot directly define correct shape. Minimizing holes / connected components can fill valid gaps and join distinct objects.

All 2400 existing alpha images were evaluated; 12 new semantic tests and 10 existing tests passed. No trainer changes or new optimization occurred. P95 here describes full-scene alpha, not an object completeness rate. [26]
Fixed cameras2/86/188 each scan 200 times; the original path is retained. C1/T1/O1 total 2400 native renders. [25]

Camera / time pairs matching observations are more complete. Away from them, RGB and alpha show streaks, fragments and gaps. Association and flow training do not remove this pattern.

There is one camera per time, not synchronized multiview imagery at each time. Training constrains Render(G(t_k), c_k); the fixed-view audit tests Render(G(t_k), c_fixed). More model-generated views add consistency checks but no independent true-motion evidence. [25]

Major artifacts also occur in native 1600x900 images, not just resized images or compressed video. All three fixed-camera matrix fingerprints stay unchanged; all 16 videos decode for 200 frames each. Manual review covers predefined key frames and contact sheets, not every pixel of all 2400 images. No independent fixed novel-view GT exists, so no surrogate PSNR or true 3D surface error is reported. [25]

16,092 conditional static rows, 42 anchors and 33,348 local projection observations; all 2000 camera samples match, with no learning-rate reset. EPE falls about 33.9%, but test PSNR gains only 0.0057 dB and both arms remain below original C1. Fixed views fragment; late support from the early bank stays zero. [27]
Version2: test the old-parameters / late-training explanation

A fresh seed20261103 starts from a saved step-zero state with an empty optimizer and no historical learned tensors. Both arms warm up for 15k and pass training-data binding gates before branching: S0 off / S1 on, each to total50k. The remaining 35k camera samples match exactly, retaining the full learning-rate schedule. [28]

Scratch training better tests early constraint activation, but yields no image gain here. Both arms exceeding historical C1 also reflects a new seed and run differences; the added constraints cannot claim that gain.
Naming: scratch S1 on this page is a historical experiment arm. Stage S1 below is independent static reconstruction. They are different models. [27,28,36]
Local Losses Fall; Images Still Fragment
Both arms have 88,916 points: 14624 static rows, 37 anchors and 31897 short-track observations. [28]

Figure2. Fixed camera86: S0 left, S1 right, at predefined early / middle / late times. The middle time coinciding with observation is more complete; early / late images retain streaks, layers and fragments. Proportional resizing only; no hole filling.

Early-bank contribution rises 55.80% to 58.31% early and 14.29% to 14.89% mid-sequence. Late contribution is negligible: about 1.94e-7 (raw fraction) for S0 and 0 for S1. Local constraints act, but early surfaces do not regain sustained support for late visible ducks. [28]

Completed: 35 unit tests, real GPU / Adam and resume checks, 2400 native renders, and all 200 frames of 16 videos. This weakens the old-parameters or late low-learning-rate explanation, without rejecting all scratch or alternative supervision designs. No identity recovery across occlusion is established. [28]
R0 completed and was rejected; R0a found an initial-reference issue. The next approach independently reconstructs static geometry in Stage S1. [29-31]

Hard static rows have zero time-varying center / covariance error by construction, yet 68.18% have opacity<0.01. Dynamic / unknown rows fit the images instead; fixed views still fragment. Image guards pass, geometry goals fail, and H1 is not promoted. [29]
R0a: final drift is not the whole problem

The same fixed mapping already has 7.7975 px reprojection error at the shared 15k start, versus 7.5642 px finally. The 14,624 rows come from 120 reference frames; freezing each old warp does not ensure one consistent surface. The 37 conditional tracks do not cover all static geometry. [30]
Stage S1: conditional progress in static reconstruction

4126 points are initialized from multitime training-silhouette support, with no dynamic parameters. Median opacity is 0.6584; only 0.291% are below 0.01. R0's mass transparency is not repeated, allowing conditional static initialization for S2. [31]

This is local progress. The new branch uses metadata CV cameras; historical PIDG cameras are unchanged. S1 and R0 differ in architecture, camera convention and objectives, so they are not a one-change matched ablation and do not establish accurate contact surfaces.
These are reconstruction-stage numbers. Dynamic PSNR below is each stage's native 1600x900 conditional dynamic-region validation score. [32-38]
Images / tracks improve; novel views fragment

S2 uses four fixed canonical banks and four original PIDG deformation networks, totaling 15,507 dynamic points; S1 static geometry remains frozen. Positive bounded scales and static RGB normalization repair some degeneration. Fixed86/188 still show flat sheets and streaks, frame42 mixes groups, and late physical identity remains unknown. [32]

S3's first resumed short run failed because canonical neighborhoods degenerated; this failure remains recorded. A separate fix uses current-world within-group neighborhoods and explicitly restores graph caches. The full 6k run and restoration of 136 Adam states / sampling then pass; this does not establish true stress or successful geometry. [33]
S4/S5: report failures and whether objectives activate

S4 binds 91 segments, 455 observations and 79 fixed rows. Reprojection over all observations rises 0.53684 to 0.78502 px@400, worsening 46.2%. S5 lowers it to 0.66467 px, still above S3. These are training-image correspondences, not independent geometry GT. [34,35]

Across 800 S5 conditional-interior-prior calls, active violations and nonzero losses are both 0. Synthetic sphere / plane fixtures pass a 300-step operator test, but no actual scene collision is corrected. Inter-object nonpenetration, contact forces, friction and restitution remain unverified / disabled. [35]

Formal S6 4000-step training and native evaluation are complete: track error 0.42711 px@400, 20.44% below S3; static geometry remains S1. Observed images improve, novel views fragment, and all 800 conditional-volume-prior calls remain inactive. See p31-34. [37,38]
Separate engineering completion, objective optimization, independent observational improvement and physical validity.
Yes. C1/H3 and scratch controls have high RGB scores, with important failing frames.

Do separate velocity and deformation agree?
The original separate head disagrees strongly. Trajectory-derived velocity unifies readout by construction, without automatically improving momentum residuals.
Can points be assigned to objects?
Within clear continuous segments, some points gain local object membership through image tracks and multiple banks.
Unverified. Fully hidden interactions lack independent identity cues; late support from early banks remains near zero.

No. Shared E, internal stress / residuals or zero priors do not supply material or contact ground truth.
Priority: verifiable geometry and identity evidence

1. S6 is complete: observed images and errors on 455 existing track observations improve, but fixed novel views still fragment. Accept as a conditional reconstruction final state, not complete geometry or physics success. No extra training is launched for this report. [37,38]

2. Prioritize checkable object correspondences across gaps and full-time surface support. Validate against simulator object / mesh IDs, persistent vertices or synchronized multiview data when available. Keep unsupported identity unknown; do not force nearest-point matches.

3. Use separate short controls for static references, dynamic canonical / actual footprints and camera conventions. Fixed-view proxies can screen failures, not serve as the sole correct-geometry target.

4. Once reconstruction and identity evidence stabilize, follow M0-M10 for F, constitutive consistency, shared material parameters and identifiability. Retain flags-off checks, unit tests, short training and resume evidence.

S6: Formal Metrics and Training Setup
